task.description: Step 2b of WF-03 for ISS-0421: hard-gate CODE-DESIGNER's lib/letflow/design/iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md, with independent verification of the Admission.global_cap arithmetic, the peak-platform-concurrency safety argument for maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 (design section 3b/3c), Task.async_stream fault-isolation semantics (AC1), AC4 preservation, the sequential-sweep architecture decision, absence of literal code, and whether the 3 flagged open questions are safe to leave open.

result.summary:
6 of 7 checks pass; 1 fails, and it is the safety-critical one (item 2, the peak-concurrency argument for section 3b). Full findings below.

1) ARITHMETIC CLAIM -- VERIFIED CORRECT. Read Letflow.Admission.init/1 directly (lib/letflow/admission.ex:221-222): `global_cap = max(pool_size - reserved_headroom, 1)`. Confirmed `config/dev.exs:54` sets `pool_size: 10` and `config/runtime.exs:113` sets it via `POOL_SIZE` env, default `"10"` -- both current, not stale. `@default_reserved_headroom` (admission.ex:121) is `2`. So `global_cap = 8` at current config, exactly as the design states. Confirmed via lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex:86,133 that `Letflow.Plugs.Admission` is mounted with both `pool: :global` (first plug, before Plug.Parsers) and `pool: :tenant` (after AuthPipeline) on every HTTP request, and per Admission's own moduledoc a `{:tenant, schema}` acquisition ALSO consumes a global unit (the 'composing rule') -- so the design's claim that the 8-unit cap is genuinely shared platform-wide between HTTP and Poller is correct, not asserted without support.

2) PEAK-CONCURRENCY SAFETY ARGUMENT -- FAILS. My own independent trace, not the design's narrative: the design's section 3b sets `maybe_refresh_active_instances/1`'s `max_concurrency` to a literal `2`, justified as 'exactly Admission's own reserved_headroom (2)', producing worst-case `8 (HTTP via Admission.global_cap) + 2 (this sweep) = 10 = pool_size`. This arithmetic is correct ONLY at the instant it was written, for the CURRENT config value of reserved_headroom. The design nowhere establishes that these two numbers -- Admission's `reserved_headroom` (a config value read once in Admission.init/1, independently overridable via `config :letflow, :admission, reserved_headroom:` per admission.ex:160-164, or via `start_link/1` opts) and Poller's own `max_concurrency: 2` for this one unwrapped sweep -- are locked together by any code, test, or documented invariant. They are two independently-maintained literals that the design's own safety proof requires to stay numerically identical (N must equal reserved_headroom, not merely start out equal to it). If reserved_headroom is ever reduced (e.g. to 1, to give the global pool more admittable slots) without someone remembering to also change this sweep's hardcoded max_concurrency, `global_cap` rises to 9 and the ACTUAL worst-case combined peak becomes `9 + 2 = 11 > pool_size(10)` -- an actual pool-exhaustion risk, not a hypothetical one, since maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 has zero Admission backstop and nothing else would catch this drift. This is exactly the class of cross-value lockstep hazard this same codebase already recognizes and explicitly flags elsewhere -- lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex:105-111 requires its multipart Plug.Parsers `length:` and `Letflow.Repository.Attachments.@max_upload_bytes` to 'stay numerically identical... flagged for REVIEWER' precisely because two independently-edited literals encoding one safety invariant is a known, named hazard pattern in this codebase. The ISS-0421 design does not apply that same discipline to its own two-number invariant: it documents the arithmetic as if `2` were a constant, not as a value that must be derived from or asserted equal to `Admission`'s actual reserved_headroom. Note this is DIFFERENT from the open question the design already flags in section 3b/8 ('reserved_headroom may have other, uninventoried consumers') -- that is a capacity-adequacy question the design correctly leaves open; the gap I am flagging is a correctness-invariant/maintainability gap (two numbers must move together and nothing enforces or even asserts that), which is not safe to leave to ELIXIR-DEV's judgment silently, per this project's no-partial-credit standard for a checkable, statable fact.

3) FAULT ISOLATION (AC1) -- VERIFIED SOUND. Task.async_stream/3's default `on_timeout: :exit` does terminate the calling process on a per-task timeout (confirmed against documented Task.async_stream semantics), so `on_timeout: :kill_task` is correctly required, not optional, to satisfy AC1. Separately confirmed Task.async_stream's default behavior on an unhandled raise inside a task is to also terminate the whole stream/caller (tasks are linked to the caller by default) -- `on_timeout: :kill_task` does not cover this case at all (it only governs timeouts), so the design's additional requirement of a per-task top-level rescue at the 2 flagged call sites (poll-and-fire loop, retention sweep -- both verified against poller.ex:171-175 and 235-239 to currently lack any inline rescue, unlike the other 4 sweeps at poller.ex:256-259, 328-330, 345-347, 362-364 which already have one) is necessary and correctly scoped. `zip_input_on_exit: true` is a real, correctly-described option. This mechanism genuinely achieves 'one slow/erroring tenant doesn't block others' as claimed.

4) AC4 (single query/tick) -- VERIFIED PRESERVED. Read poller.ex:169,266-281 directly: `fetch_tenant_schemas/0` has exactly one call site inside `handle_info(:tick, state)`, and the resulting `schemas` binding is threaded by reference into all 7 sweep calls (poller.ex:171-182) unchanged. The design does not touch this and correctly says so.

5) SEQUENTIAL-SWEEPS DECISION -- SOUND. The reasoning in section 2 (concurrent sweeps would cause 6 sweeps sharing one 8-slot Admission budget to cannibalize each other's grants tick-over-tick, a correctness regression on top of the safety question, and would break section 3b's own no-overlap assumption) holds and is adequately justified; no further justification needed.

6) NO LITERAL CODE -- VERIFIED CLEAN. Full read of lib/letflow/design/iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md: no defmodule/def/do-block anywhere; only prose, arithmetic, and named-accessor descriptions (matching the commit history's prior 2 reworks that already scrubbed literal Elixir from this same doc).

7) OPEN QUESTIONS -- 2 of 3 safe to leave open, 1 is superseded by finding #2 above. The Task.Supervisor question (no async-orphan risk since the calling process blocks until the stream drains) and the sweep_task_timeout_ms-vs-poll_interval_ms ordering question are genuinely judgment calls with reasonable defaults given, safe for ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER to confirm rather than block on. The reserved_headroom-inventory question is a capacity question, separately safe to leave open. But finding #2's lockstep-invariant gap is NOT safe to leave open -- it is a checkable, statable design fact (two numbers must be provably equal, always) that the design should resolve, not defer.
result.routing: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER (rework iteration 1) for lib/letflow/design/iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md. Required fix, precise: section 3b/7 must not present `max_concurrency: 2` for maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 as an independent hardcoded literal that merely happens to equal Admission's current reserved_headroom. Pick and specify ONE of: (a) add a public accessor to lib/letflow/admission.ex (e.g. `Letflow.Admission.reserved_headroom/0` or `.global_cap/0`, read fresh, no GenServer round-trip needed if reserved_headroom/pool_size are exposed as plain config reads mirroring Letflow.Scheduler's own 'read config fresh' convention already cited elsewhere in this same design) so Poller's own bound is DERIVED from Admission's actual current value at call time, making the invariant impossible to silently violate; or (b) if (a) is rejected for a stated reason, add an explicit MUST-match invariant statement to both lib/letflow/admission.ex's reserved_headroom definition and the new Poller code comment, mirroring api_pipeline.ex:105-111's own precedent for exactly this hazard class ('these two numbers must change together, flagged for REVIEWER'), AND specify a concrete enforcement mechanism (e.g. a test asserting `Letflow.Scheduler.sweep 3b bound == Application.get_env(:letflow, :admission, [])[:reserved_headroom] || 2` so a future edit to one without the other fails CI, not just a code comment trusting a human to remember). Do not leave this as a silent hardcoded match with no stated coupling -- that is the exact gap this rework targets. All 6 other checks (Admission arithmetic, fault isolation, AC4 preservation, sequential-sweep architecture, no literal code, remaining 2 open questions) passed and do not need rework.

next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER to add the reserved_headroom/max_concurrency lockstep fix (accessor-derived bound or explicit enforced MUST-match invariant) to lib/letflow/design/iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md section 3b, then re-route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for re-check.

gate_history.notes: Admission.global_cap arithmetic (pool_size 10 - reserved_headroom 2 = 8) independently verified correct against admission.ex/api_pipeline.ex/config. Peak-concurrency safety argument in section 3b fails: max_concurrency:2 for maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 is a hardcoded literal that must stay equal to Admission's reserved_headroom for the 8+2=10 proof to hold, but nothing derives or enforces that equality -- a future independent change to reserved_headroom would silently break the pool-exhaustion safety bound. All other checks (fault isolation, AC4, sequential-sweep decision, no literal code, 2 of 3 open questions) passed.
